title: The complexity of identifying a graph by Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
main_claim: Deciding whether WLdim(G) <= k, with G given by its adjacency matrix and k in binary (or unary), is EXPTIME-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
coverage: Read all 7 sections in full. Checked: Lemma 2.1, the WL to bijective (k+1)-slot game equivalence (forward needs k>=2 so any two slots survive one deletion), monotonicity, and the EXPTIME upper bound (accept when k>=n). Prop 3.x (mate reconstruction): degree intervals I_j are disjoint and above 1, leaf counting, and the exclusion of edges between color classes that are never adjacent. Local iso of each block piece uses <=26 marked vertices, which fits in K>=33 slots, and coordinate flips turn the square RHS into beta_B. Iso <-> global offsets. Prop 4.1 (image consistency): the consistency test needs 3 slots, and site-ring -> square-ring -> site-ring transfer with r+1 slots, where vertical readouts cancel. Lemma 4.3 (cycle lifting): rectangular differences need r>=3, alpha_i=gamma_{i-1}, and sum c_i=0 gives the C_i. Prop 4.4 converse: internal h_s, residual g_i, Y_i on the source labels. Section 5: type-support tree; wrapping lemma (c_{i-1}=c_i, the aligned-label argument, uniqueness of the address when |U|<=r+1); admissible shifts and the internal Q-set consistency for arms at the first or last endpoint and for loop wires; exact projection (restriction, lifting from a wrapping old component, the marker-potential gauge s_v g_t on nonwrapping components); and Duplicator's ownership-based bijection. Section 7: the buffer forces singleton propagation; AND ports; broadcast via coordinate flips reaches every address; self-connections give s(h_P)=Delta_l1+Delta_l2+Delta_l3, which is in row-sum form; buffer and dummy functions. Rejection: the two A self-loops contradict each other at every address, and the image sets ({0} for true gates, F for false ones, product sets for AND gates, buffer sets {(u,v): u+v in D'+b}) satisfy all comparisons. Size is O((r+1)^12). Not re-verified: the companion compilation theorem [VariableWL, Prop 3.2], which is used as a black box (rank410 sibling reported no gap in its product schemas).
sibling_notes: Family 133 siblings (rank410 VariableWL, rank401, rank259) all report no_gap_found. This paper imports only the uniform product-circuit compiler from VariableWL (Prop 3.2), which rank410 checked. The marker-potential gauge and the wrapping/address lemma closely parallel the companion's exact-projection argument and were re-checked here independently, including the new identification-specific Q-set conditions.
